intro: でも is で plus も: "even with this". It takes one thing and says the statement still holds for it. That gives "even X" for an extreme case, "X or something" for a loose suggestion, and, after a question word, "any X at all".

skills.rule: N でも means "even N": the statement holds even for this extreme case, the one where you would least expect it.
skills.explain:
でも after a noun picks an extreme case and says the claim reaches it: この問題は子どもでも分かる "Even a child can understand this problem", so anyone can. It replaces が, を and は (子どもでも, not 子どもがでも), and it follows other particles: ここからでも見える "you can see it even from here".

It works with negatives when the extreme is a strong case: 先生でも分からない "even the teacher doesn't know". But for "not even [the most basic thing]" use さえ or も: ひらがなさえ読めない "he can't even read hiragana". In that sentence でも sounds wrong.

Keep the neighbours apart. Plain も only adds: 子どもも分かる "children understand too". でも makes the noun the unlikely limit. さえ is a stronger, more bookish "even". After a verb or adjective, 〜ても / 〜でも (読んでも, 静かでも) is the "even if" conditional, a separate skill, and sentence-initial でも means "but".
patterns: [particle] でも  (ここからでも, 日本にでも)
N でも [negative]  (strong case: 先生でも分からない)

examples.jp: この問題[もんだい]は子[こ]ども{でも}分[わ]かります。
examples.en: Even a child can understand this problem.

examples.jp: 日曜日[にちようび]{でも}この店[みせ]は開[あ]いています。
examples.en: This shop is open even on Sundays.

examples.jp: 雨[あめ]の日[ひ]{でも}毎朝[まいあさ]走[はし]っています。
examples.en: I run every morning, even on rainy days.

examples.jp: ここから{でも}富士山[ふじさん]が見[み]えます。
examples.en: You can see Mt Fuji even from here.

examples.jp: 先生[せんせい]{でも}分[わ]からない漢字[かんじ]があります。
examples.en: There are kanji that even teachers don't know.

contrast.note: も adds one more: 子どもも "children too". でも marks the unlikely limit: 子どもでも "even children".
さえ is the stronger, more formal "even", and the one to use for "not even the basics": ひらがなさえ読めない.

mistakes.bad: 子[こ]どもが{でも}分[わ]かります。
mistakes.good: 子[こ]ども{でも}分[わ]かります。
mistakes.note: でも replaces が, を and は. Only particles like に, から, と stay in front of it.

mistakes.bad: 弟[おとうと]はひらがな{でも}読[よ]めません。
mistakes.good: 弟[おとうと]はひらがな{さえ}読[よ]めません。
mistakes.note: "Not even [the easiest thing]" takes さえ (or も); でも is for a strong case where the claim still holds.

skills.tip: Picture the most unlikely case and say "even": でも. Just "also": も. "Not even the basics": さえ.

skills.rule: In an offer, invitation or wish, N でも means "N or something": it proposes N as one easy option.
skills.explain:
In invitations, offers, requests and wishes, でも after a noun means "N, or something like that": お茶でも飲みませんか "Shall we have some tea or something?" The speaker is not insisting on tea; でも keeps the idea light and easy to turn down, which is why it is so common in invitations.

It replaces を and が, and follows other particles: 散歩にでも行きませんか "Shall we go for a walk or something?", 週末にでも会いましょう "Let's meet at the weekend or so". It belongs with forward-looking forms: 〜ませんか, 〜ましょう, 〜(よ)う, 〜たい, 〜てください. In a report of what already happened (昨日お茶でも飲みました) it does not fit; there you name the thing with を.

The boundary: お茶を飲みませんか is also correct, but it invites to tea specifically and sounds more pointed. お茶も would mean "tea as well". The casual equivalent is なんか (お茶なんかどう?), the formal one など (お茶などいかがですか).
patterns: N でも [〜ませんか / 〜ましょう / 〜(よ)う]
N に でも 行きませんか
N でも [〜たい / 〜てください]

examples.jp: お茶[ちゃ]{でも}飲[の]みませんか。
examples.en: Shall we have some tea or something?

examples.jp: 映画[えいが]{でも}見[み]に行[い]こうか。
examples.en: Shall we go and see a film or something?

examples.jp: 週末[しゅうまつ]に{でも}会[あ]いましょう。
examples.en: Let's meet at the weekend or sometime.

examples.jp: 暇[ひま]なら、散歩[さんぽ]に{でも}行[い]きませんか。
examples.en: If you're free, shall we go for a walk or something?

examples.jp: 疲[つか]れたから、甘[あま]いもの{でも}食[た]べたいな。
examples.en: I'm tired, so I feel like something sweet.

examples.jp: 時間[じかん]があったら、電話[でんわ]{でも}ください。
examples.en: If you have time, give me a call or something.

contrast.note: お茶を飲みませんか invites to tea specifically. お茶でも offers tea as one easy option and sounds softer.
お茶も飲みませんか means "won't you have tea as well?", adding to something already offered; でも offers a loose example.

mistakes.bad: お茶[ちゃ]を{でも}飲[の]みませんか。
mistakes.good: お茶[ちゃ]{でも}飲[の]みませんか。
mistakes.note: でも replaces を (and が). Only particles like に stay in front of it.

mistakes.bad: 昨日[きのう]は友達[ともだち]とお茶[ちゃ]{でも}飲[の]みました。
mistakes.good: 昨日[きのう]は友達[ともだち]とお茶[ちゃ]{を}飲[の]みました。
mistakes.note: "Or something" でも belongs in suggestions and wishes, not in reports of what happened.

skills.tip: Could you add "or something" to an invitation? Swap を for でも.

skills.rule: Question word + でも means "any ... at all": 何でも anything, いつでも any time, 誰でも anyone, どこでも anywhere.
skills.explain:
でも after a question word turns it into a positive, all-inclusive "any": 何でも食べます "I'll eat anything", いつでも来てください "Come any time". It works with 誰, 何 (read なん: なんでも), いつ, どこ, どれ, どちら, and with question word + noun: どの店でも "at any shop", どんな人でも "any kind of person".

Learn it as one of three sets. Question word + も with a negative means "no...": 何も食べません "I don't eat anything", 誰もいない "there's no one here" (but いつも "always" and どちらも "both" are positive). Question word + か means "some...", one you don't specify: 何か食べたい "I want to eat something", 誰か来た? "Did someone come?" Question word + でも means "any, whichever you pick".

Particles: が and を disappear (誰でもできる, 何でも聞いて). に, と and から stay and come before でも: どこにでもある "it's everywhere", 誰にでも優しい "kind to everyone". で for a place or means is usually absorbed: どの店でも売っている.

examples.jp: 何[なん]{でも}食[た]べます。
いつ{でも}遊[あそ]びに来[き]てください。
この仕事[しごと]は誰[だれ]{でも}できます。
コンビニはどこに{でも}あります。
このお菓子[かし]はどの店[みせ]{でも}売[う]っています。
examples.en: These sweets are sold in any shop.

examples.jp: 分[わ]からないことがあったら、何[なん]{でも}聞[き]いてください。
examples.en: If anything is unclear, ask me whatever you like.

contrast.note: Question word + も goes with a negative: 何も食べない "I eat nothing". でも goes with a positive: 何でも食べる "I eat anything".
Question word + か is "some, one I don't specify": 誰か来た? "Did someone come?" でも is "anyone at all, whoever it is".

mistakes.good: 何[なん]{でも}食[た]べます。
mistakes.note: 何も needs a negative verb. For "I'll eat anything" with a positive verb, use 何でも.

mistakes.bad: 誰[だれ]{でも}来[き]ましたか。
mistakes.good: 誰[だれ]{か}来[き]ましたか。
mistakes.note: Asking whether some unspecified person came takes か; でも means "anyone at all" and does not fit a yes/no question about one event.

mistakes.bad: 誰[だれ]{でも}に優[やさ]しい人[ひと]です。
mistakes.good: 誰[だれ]に{でも}優[やさ]しい人[ひと]です。
mistakes.note: に stays and comes before でも.

skills.tip: 何か some, 何も...ない none, 何でも any at all. Positive verb plus "whatever it is"? でも.
